biology is the study of life
amphibious means having a double life
items.exampleCN: amphibious 意为「过双重生活的」

items.meaning: an oval theater open all around
able to use both hands equally
items.meaningCN: 双手都灵巧的；平行前缀对照
模棱两可的；易混词对照

definition_zh: n. 圆形露天剧场；（美）阶梯式讲堂；环形阶梯座位区
definition_en: An open circular building with tiers of seats rising around a central space; also a lecture hall or a valley shaped like one.
core_image: 一圈圈石阶围着中央那块空地
scene: 学生们坐在山坡的阶梯座位上听露天讲座。The lecture was held in a natural amphitheatre.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里不是古罗马建筑，而是形状像圆形剧场的天然山坡阶梯座位区，讲座就在那里举行。

pos.zh: 圆形露天剧场；阶梯式讲堂

senses.title: The ancient circular building
senses.definition: an open oval or circular structure with rising tiers of seats around a central arena
senses.definitionCN: 露天的椭圆形或圆形建筑，中央竞技场四周环绕着逐层升高的座位
senses.example: The amphitheatre could hold twenty thousand spectators.
senses.exampleCN: 这座圆形剧场能容纳两万名观众。
senses.why: Greek amphi- means on both sides and theatron means a place for seeing, so the word names a place where you can see from every side.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 amphi- 意为「在两边」，theatron 意为「观看之所」，所以这个词命名的是一个从每一侧都能观看的地方。

senses.title: Any tiered ring of seats
senses.definition: a lecture hall, hillside or valley whose seats or slopes rise in a semicircle
senses.definitionCN: 座位或坡面呈半圆形逐层升高的讲堂、山坡或谷地
senses.example: The village sits in a natural amphitheatre of hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄坐落在群山环抱的天然环形谷地中。
senses.why: The shape, not the stone, carries the meaning: once the tiers curve around a centre, the name transfers to lecture halls and landscapes.
senses.whyCN: 承载含义的是形状而非石材：只要阶梯围绕一个中心弯曲，这个名称就转移到讲堂与地形上。

intro.en: Amphitheatre is Greek amphitheatron, from amphi-, on both sides, and theatron, a place for seeing. Latin took it as amphitheatrum, and English kept both the -tre and -ter spellings.
intro.cn: amphitheatre 来自希腊语 amphitheatron，由 amphi-「在两边」与 theatron「观看之所」构成。拉丁语借为 amphitheatrum，英语保留了 -tre 与 -ter 两种拼写。

items.en: Amphi meant on both sides or around, and appears in amphibious and amphora as well as this word.
items.cn: amphi 意为「在两边、环绕」，除本词外也出现在 amphibious 与 amphora 中。

items.en: Theatron meant a place for seeing, from theaomai, to look at. A theatre was originally the seating, not the stage.
items.cn: theatron 意为「观看之所」，来自 theaomai「观看」。剧院最初指的是座位区，而不是舞台。

items.en: Greek amphitheatron joined the two pieces for a structure where spectators surround the action instead of facing it from one side.
items.cn: 希腊语 amphitheatron 把两个部件拼合，指观众环绕而非单侧面对表演场地的建筑。

items.en: Latin amphitheatrum named the Roman buildings, and the ruins kept the word alive across Europe long after the games stopped.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amphitheatrum 指那些罗马建筑，竞技停止很久之后，遗址仍让这个词在欧洲各地流传。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, keeps -tre in Britain and -ter in America, and extends it to any tiered semicircle.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入该词，英国用 -tre、美国用 -ter，并把它扩展到任何阶梯半圆形空间。

note.en: The look-alike group handles the two spellings and the near opening amphora; the near-meaning group lists other venues built around a centre.
note.cn: 形近组处理两种拼写与开头相近的 amphora；近义组列出其他围绕中心而建的场所。

entries.definition: The same word in American spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: Arranged in rising curved tiers.
entries.definitionCN: 呈逐层升高弧形排列的。

entries.definition: A building for plays, seats facing one way.
entries.definitionCN: 演剧的建筑，座位朝一个方向。

entries.definition: A two-handled ancient jar.
entries.definitionCN: 一种双耳古代陶罐。

entries.definition: The open space where events take place.
entries.definitionCN: 举行活动的开阔场地。

entries.definition: A large sports ground with tiered seats.
entries.definitionCN: 带阶梯座位的大型运动场。

entries.definition: The part of a hall where the audience sits.
entries.definitionCN: 厅内观众就座的部分。

entries.definition: A very large ancient amphitheatre.
entries.definitionCN: 极大的古代圆形剧场。

normalIntro.en: Amphitheatre is amphi plus theatre: a theatre you can watch from every side.
normalIntro.cn: amphitheatre 就是 amphi 加 theatre：一个从每一侧都能观看的剧院。

normal.en: A theatre faces one way; an amphitheatre wraps around.
normal.cn: theatre 朝一个方向，amphitheatre 环绕一圈。

normal.en: British spelling ends -tre, American ends -ter.
normal.cn: 英式拼写以 -tre 结尾，美式以 -ter 结尾。

normal.en: The plural is amphitheatres, with a plain s.
normal.cn: 复数是 amphitheatres，直接加 s。

normal.en: A natural amphitheatre is a bowl of hills, not a building.
normal.cn: natural amphitheatre 指碗状群山，不是建筑。

normal.en: Do not confuse amphitheatre with amphora, a jar.
normal.cn: 别把 amphitheatre 与 amphora「陶罐」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture stone rings rising around a patch of sand.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈圈石阶围绕一片沙地升起。

abstract.en: Imagine a hillside where every student can see the speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象一片山坡，每个学生都能看见讲者。

abstract.en: Think of a village held in the palm of a valley.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄被托在谷地的手心里。

examples.en: The amphitheatre survives almost intact after two thousand years.
examples.cn: 这座圆形剧场历经两千年几乎完好无损。

examples.en: Concerts are staged in the amphitheatre each summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天都在露天剧场举办音乐会。

examples.en: The medical school built a small amphitheatre for demonstrations.
examples.cn: 医学院建了一间小型阶梯讲堂用于演示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：amphi「两边、环绕」+ theatre「剧院」——座位绕着中央转一圈的剧院，就是圆形剧场。

root: 希腊语 amphi「环绕」+ theatron「观看之所」构成 amphitheatron，拉丁语借为 amphitheatrum，英语作 amphitheatre（美 amphitheater），字面即「四面都能观看的场所」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one shape: the Roman stone ring, and any hillside or hall that copies its curved tiers.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个形状：罗马的石环，以及任何模仿其弧形阶梯的山坡或厅堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stone rings rising around one open centre
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈圈石阶围着一块开阔中心升起

branches.en: A Roman ruin with sand in the middle.
branches.cn: 中央铺沙的罗马遗址。

branches.en: Twenty thousand seats facing inward.
branches.cn: 两万个朝内的座位。

branches.en: A lecture hall with curved rows.
branches.cn: 座位呈弧形排列的讲堂。

branches.en: A valley that holds a village like a bowl.
branches.cn: 像碗一样托住村庄的谷地。

branches.en: The same curve, in stone then in land.
branches.cn: 同一条弧线，先在石头上，再在地形上。

intro.en: Amphitheatre keeps amphi- and the seeing root thea-, and the same pieces build theatre, audience and auditorium.
intro.cn: amphitheatre 保留 amphi- 与「观看」词根 thea-，同样的部件还构成 theatre、audience 与 auditorium。

latinIntro.en: Greek amphitheatron became Latin amphitheatrum; the -um ending was dropped in French and English, leaving -tre or -ter.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 amphitheatron 变成拉丁语 amphitheatrum；-um 词尾在法语与英语中脱落，留下 -tre 或 -ter。

latinEntries.meaning: a place seen from all sides

definition_zh: 充足的；宽敞的；丰满的
definition_en: more than enough in size, quantity, or space
core_image: 撑满整个画框的宽大衣袍，处处有余
scene: 法官给双方律师留足申辩时间。The judge allowed ample time for both lawyers to present their arguments.
sceneCN: 这里的 ample 是「充足的」（第 1 个义项：绰绰有余）；句意是法官给双方律师留了充足的时间陈述论点。

collocations.zh: 丰满的身形；宽大的格局

derivatives.zh: 由 ample 词根 ampl- 派生，义为「放大；增强；扩充」
由 amplify 加名词后缀 -er 构成，义为「放大器」
由 ampl- 加后缀 -itude 构成，义为「振幅；广大；充足」
由 amplify 派生，义为「放大；扩充；详述」

senses.title: More than enough in quantity
senses.definition: as much or as many as needed and more; more than sufficient
senses.definitionCN: 足够且有余，超出需要的量
senses.example: There is ample evidence to convict him.
senses.exampleCN: 证据充足，足以给他定罪。
senses.why: The Latin root ampl- means large; what fills beyond the required line is ample.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 ampl- 意为「大」；超出所需刻度、漫出来的量就是充足。

senses.title: Large in size or width
senses.definition: physically large, wide, or capacious
senses.definitionCN: 面积大、空间宽敞，形容房间、衣袍等实物尺寸
senses.example: The library has ample reading rooms with high windows.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆有宽敞的阅览室，窗户高亮。
senses.why: Largeness of quantity extends naturally to largeness of physical extent.
senses.whyCN: 量的「大」自然延伸到形体的「大」：能装得下更多就是宽敞。

senses.title: Full and generous in shape
senses.titleCN: 丰满的；宽松的（体形或衣物）
senses.definition: describing a full figure or loose, generously cut clothing
senses.definitionCN: 形容体形丰腴或衣物剪裁宽大有余
senses.example: She wore an ample robe that swept the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着一件曳地的宽大衣袍。
senses.why: A body or garment that spills generously beyond the frame shows the same largeness as an ample supply.
senses.whyCN: 体态或衣物丰盈地漫出轮廓，与供应漫出需求是同一种「大」，故引申为丰满、宽松。

intro.en: Ample comes from Latin amplus, large or spacious, of uncertain older origin.
intro.cn: ample 来自拉丁语 amplus「大的、宽敞的」，更早来源不确定。

items.en: Possible links to a root meaning to fill or spread exist, but the chain is uncertain.
items.cn: 或与表示「充满、铺展」的词根有关，但演变链条存疑。

items.en: Latin amplus meant large, spacious, or honorable; amplificare meant to enlarge.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amplus 意为「大的、宽敞的、尊贵的」；amplificare 意为「放大」。

items.en: Old French ample kept the sense of wide and extensive.
items.cn: 古法语 ample 保留「宽阔、广博」之义。

items.en: English adopted ample in the 15th century for generous in size and quantity.
items.cn: 英语于 15 世纪借入 ample，表示尺寸与数量上的宽绰。

items.en: The word now covers sufficiency, spaciousness, and generous body or garment shapes.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖充足、宽敞以及体态衣物之丰盈宽大。

note.en: Ample sits between enough and abundant, and is paired with its noun-family amplify and amplitude.
note.cn: ample 介于 enough 与 abundant 之间，并与同族的 amplify、amplitude 配套。

entries.definition: to make larger or louder
entries.definitionCN: 放大、增强，与 ample 同出拉丁语 amplus

entries.definition: largeness; the height of a wave
entries.definitionCN: 广大；振幅，与 ample 同根的名词

entries.definition: a device that increases volume or signal
entries.definitionCN: 放大器，amplify 的施动者名词

entries.definition: to walk slowly
entries.definitionCN: 缓行，与 ample 只是拼写相近，词源不同（行走 vs 大）

entries.definition: existing in large quantities
entries.definitionCN: 丰富的、大量的，程度比 ample 更强

entries.definition: available in large amounts
entries.definitionCN: 丰富的，侧重供应充足

entries.definition: larger or more than usual
entries.definitionCN: 宽厚的、慷慨的，兼有量足与心善两义

entries.definition: able to hold much
entries.definitionCN: 容量大的，对应宽敞义项

entries.definition: barely enough
entries.definitionCN: barely enough 不足的、仅有的，直接反义

normalIntro.en: The ampl- family makes ample easy to hold in memory.
normalIntro.cn: ampl- 词族让 ample 好记。

normal.en: ampl- is the Latin root of large.
normal.cn: ampl- 是拉丁语「大」的词根。

normal.en: amplify adds -fy, meaning to make large.
normal.cn: amplify 加 -fy，表示「使变大」。

normal.en: amplitude adds -itude, meaning largeness as a measure.
normal.cn: amplitude 加 -itude，表示作为度量的「广度、振幅」。

normal.en: ample food and ample time both mean more than needed.
normal.cn: ample food 与 ample time 都指超出所需。

normal.en: ample is stronger than enough but softer than abundant.
normal.cn: ample 比 enough 强、比 abundant 委婉。

abstract.en: See a robe that billows well past the chair it hangs on.
abstract.cn: 想象一件袍子鼓胀开来，远超所搭的椅子。

abstract.en: Watch a table where every plate is full and no guest reaches twice.
abstract.cn: 想象满桌的餐盘，客人无需二次伸手。

abstract.en: Feel a timeline that stretches far beyond the deadline.
abstract.cn: 感受时间轴远远越过了截止线的从容。

examples.en: You will have ample opportunity to ask questions.
examples.cn: 你将有充足的机会提问。

examples.en: The hotel offers ample parking for guests.
examples.cn: 酒店为客人提供宽敞的停车场。

examples.en: He is a man of ample build and easy manners.
examples.cn: 他体格丰硕，举止从容。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安蒲」——安安稳稳铺开的席面比客人还多，铺得漫出来就是 ample：充足、宽敞。

root: 拉丁语 amplus「大的、宽敞的」，词根 ampl-「大」；词源更早阶段来源不确定。同族词 amplify（放大）、amplitude（振幅）、amplifier（放大器）。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from more-than-enough quantity, through wide physical space, to generous body or garment shapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从「超过所需的量」出发，经「宽大的物理空间」，延伸到「丰盈的体态与宽绰的衣物」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: largeness that spills past every needed line
core.cn: 核心意象：漫过一切所需刻度的「大」

branches.en: Supply beyond the need line
branches.cn: 越过需求线的供应，即充足

branches.en: Quantity largeness turned into space largeness
branches.cn: 量的大转为空间的大

branches.en: Rooms and halls that hold everything easily
branches.cn: 轻松容纳一切的房间与大厅

branches.en: Forms that spill past their outline
branches.cn: 漫出轮廓的体态与衣袍

branches.en: Generosity felt both in amount and in shape
branches.cn: 在数量与形状上同样可感的宽绰

intro.en: Ample stands on the single Latin root ampl-, large.
intro.cn: ample 建立在拉丁语词根 ampl-「大」之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin amplus heads the ampl- family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 amplus 领衔 ampl- 词族。

definition_zh: 放大（声音、信号）；增强；详述；扩充；夸大
definition_en: to make larger, stronger or louder; to expand in detail
core_image: 一只小喇叭把耳语推成一屋子都听得见的声音
scene: 礼堂后排听不清，工作人员把台上的小盒子调高了一档。A small box on the desk can amplify the speaker's voice for the back rows.
sceneCN: 这里指把声音放大（第 1 个义项：使声音变响）；句意为桌上的小盒子把讲者的声音放大，供后排听清。

pos.zh: 放大；增强；详述；扩充；夸大

senses.title: To make sound louder
senses.definition: to increase the volume of sound
senses.definitionCN: 提高声音的音量
senses.example: The hall amplifies every whisper.
senses.exampleCN: 这间大厅会把每一声耳语放大。
senses.why: Amplificare joined amplus, large, with facere, to make, so the word first meant to make something large.
senses.whyCN: amplificare 把 amplus「大的」与 facere「做」结合，因此这个词最早意为「使变大」。

senses.title: To strengthen a signal
senses.definition: to raise the strength of an electrical or radio signal
senses.definitionCN: 提高电信号或无线电信号的强度
senses.example: The repeater amplifies the weak signal.
senses.exampleCN: 中继器把微弱信号增强。
senses.why: Electronics gave the old word a measurable quantity to enlarge.
senses.whyCN: 电子学给了这个旧词一个可测量的「量」去放大。

senses.title: To intensify an effect
senses.definition: to make an effect stronger or more vivid
senses.definitionCN: 使效果更强、更鲜明
senses.example: Cold air amplifies the smell of the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 冷空气让海的味道更浓。
senses.why: Once size becomes strength, anything with intensity can be amplified.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「大」变成「强」，任何有强度的事物都能被放大。

senses.title: To expand in detail
senses.definition: to add detail to a statement or theme
senses.definitionCN: 给陈述或主题补充细节
senses.example: The speaker amplified her point with two examples.
senses.exampleCN: 讲者用两个例子详述了她的观点。
senses.why: Rhetoric used the word for filling out a theme, making it large in words.
senses.whyCN: 修辞学用这个词表示把主题铺开，使其在言辞上变大。

senses.title: To exaggerate
senses.definition: to make something seem larger or worse than it is
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物显得比实际更大或更糟
senses.example: The report amplifies the danger beyond the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把危险夸大到证据之外。
senses.why: The same enlarging act becomes a fault when it outruns the facts.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「放大」动作一旦超出事实，就成了过失。

senses.title: To multiply DNA
senses.definition: to make many copies of a DNA sequence
senses.definitionCN: 把一段脱氧核糖核酸序列复制成许多份
senses.example: The lab amplifies a short fragment of the gene.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室扩增了该基因的一小段。
senses.why: Molecular biology uses amplification for copying, an exact technical enlargement.
senses.whyCN: 分子生物学用「扩增」表示复制，是一种精确的技术性放大。

senses.title: To raise current or voltage
senses.definition: to increase the amplitude of an electrical wave
senses.definitionCN: 增大电波的振幅
senses.example: The circuit amplifies the current before it reaches the coil.
senses.exampleCN: 电路在电流到达线圈之前将其放大。
senses.why: The word amplitude itself comes from the same large-stem.
senses.whyCN: amplitude 一词本身也出自同一个表示「大」的词干。

senses.title: To fill out a rhetorical theme
senses.definition: to develop a theme at length for effect
senses.definitionCN: 为效果而把一个主题长时间展开
senses.example: The old manuals teach students to amplify a proverb.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时手册教学生把一句谚语铺陈成文。
senses.why: Ancient rhetoric named this exercise amplification, and English kept the verb.
senses.whyCN: 古代修辞学把这套练习称为铺陈，英语保留了动词。

intro.en: Amplify comes from Latin amplificare, to enlarge, from amplus, large, plus facere, to make. The direct source is clear; the origin of amplus itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: amplify 来自拉丁 amplificare「使变大」，由 amplus「大的」与 facere「做」构成。直接来源清楚；amplus 本身的来源不确定。

items.en: Amplus meant large, spacious or ample; its deeper origin is a reconstruction and is source uncertain.
items.cn: amplus 意为大的、宽敞的、充足的；其更深来源属重构，来源不确定。

items.en: The combining form -ficare comes from facere, to make, so amplificare is to make large.
items.cn: 组合形式 -ficare 来自 facere「做」，因此 amplificare 就是「使变大」。

items.en: The verb meant to enlarge, increase or widen, and rhetoric used it for expanding a theme.
items.cn: 这个动词意为扩大、增加、拓宽，修辞学用它表示展开主题。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun amplifier was coined for devices that raise signal strength in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 名词 amplifier 在二十世纪被造出，指提高信号强度的装置。

items.en: The same verb now names the copying of DNA, where enlargement is exact multiplication.
items.cn: 同一个动词如今命名 DNA 的复制，那里的「放大」是精确的倍增。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin large-making stem; the second group names ways of adding size, strength or detail.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「使变大」的词干；第二组是增加规模、强度或细节的近义说法。

entries.definition: The act of enlarging sound, signal or detail.
entries.definitionCN: 放大声音、信号或细节的行为。

entries.definition: A device that raises the strength of a signal.
entries.definitionCN: 提高信号强度的装置。

entries.definition: The size of a wave's swing, from the same large-stem.
entries.definitionCN: 波摆动的幅度，出自同一「大」词干。

entries.definition: More than enough in size or supply.
entries.definitionCN: 在规模或供给上绰绰有余。

entries.definition: To make something look bigger, especially through a lens.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物看起来更大，尤指通过透镜。

entries.definition: To make stronger in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 使程度更强。

entries.definition: To grow larger in size or scope.
entries.definitionCN: 在规模或范围上变大。

entries.definition: To raise or push up, often a signal or level.
entries.definitionCN: 提高、推高，常指信号或水平。

entries.definition: To describe something as larger than it is.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物说得比实际更大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin parts, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Amplificare is amplus plus facere: to make large.
normal.cn: amplificare 是 amplus 加 facere：使变大。

normal.en: The amplifier is the device, and amplification is the act.
normal.cn: amplifier 是装置，amplification 是行为。

normal.en: The word runs from sound to signal to feeling to detail to genetic copying.
normal.cn: 这个词从声音走到信号、感受、细节，再到基因复制。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: amplify the sound, amplify a signal, amplify a point.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：放大声音、增强信号、详述要点。

normal.en: Amplify is not augment: one magnifies what is there, the other adds more to it.
normal.cn: amplify 不是 augment：前者放大已有之物，后者往里添更多。

abstract.en: Amplify is a bell that turns a small tap into a sound across the valley.
abstract.cn: 放大是一口钟，把轻轻一碰变成满谷的声音。

abstract.en: The same act can serve truth or falsehood, depending on what is fed in.
abstract.cn: 同一个放大动作既能服务真相，也能服务谎言，取决于输入什么。

abstract.en: To amplify is to make a thing more itself, not to make it another thing.
abstract.cn: 放大是让事物更像它自己，而不是变成别的东西。

examples.en: The microphone can amplify a voice without changing its tone.
examples.cn: 麦克风能把声音放大，却不改变音色。

examples.en: The lost keys seemed to amplify the worry of the whole family.
examples.cn: 钥匙丢了，全家的担忧仿佛被放大了。

examples.en: The essay uses three pages to amplify one short proverb.
examples.cn: 这篇文章用三页篇幅铺陈一句短谚语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安普利法艾」——安个小喇叭，声音放到最大：放大

root: 拉丁 amplificare「使变大」← amplus「大的、宽敞的」+ -ficare（来自 facere「做」）。amplus 更深来源属重构，来源不确定；英语十五世纪借入，确切首见年代不确定。同族 amplitude、ample 与 amplifier 共用「大」的词干；现代又用于电子信号与 DNA 扩增。与 augment 不同：amplify 放大已有之物，augment 另行添加。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses enlarge sound, signal, effect, detail, a claim, DNA, current and a rhetorical theme.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分别放大声音、信号、效果、细节、说法、脱氧核糖核酸、电流与修辞主题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small horn that turns a whisper into a room-filling sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小喇叭把耳语变成满屋都听得见的声音。

branches.en: THE SOUND AND THE CURRENT: louder volume and a larger electrical swing.
branches.cn: 声音与电流：更大的音量与更大的电波振幅。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL: a weak carrier made strong enough to travel.
branches.cn: 信号：把微弱载波增强到能传远。

branches.en: THE STRONGER EFFECT: intensity raised, and a claim pushed past the facts.
branches.cn: 更强的效果：强度被提高，说法被推到事实之外。

branches.en: THE FULLER THEME: a point filled out and an old rhetorical exercise.
branches.cn: 更饱满的主题：被补充细节的要点与古老的修辞练习。

branches.en: THE COPIED GENE: exact multiplication in the laboratory.
branches.cn: 被复制的基因：实验室里的精确倍增。

intro.en: Amplify is Latin amplificare, with amplus and facere both visible inside the verb.
intro.cn: amplify 是拉丁 amplificare，动词内部两个构件 amplus 与 facere 都看得见。

latinIntro.en: Amplus supplies the size, -ficare supplies the making, and the noun amplification keeps the act.
latinIntro.cn: amplus 提供「大」，-ficare 提供「做」，名词 amplification 保留这一行为。

items.example: The adjective supplies the size that is to be increased.
items.exampleCN: 形容词提供待增大的规模。

items.example: The verb supplies the making in -ficare.
items.exampleCN: 动词在 -ficare 中提供「制造」。

items.example: The form turns an adjective into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式把形容词变成「使…」的动词。

items.example: Latin already used it for widening and for rhetoric.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语已用它表示拓宽与修辞铺陈。

items.example: The noun names the act rather than the device.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名行为，而非装置。

items.meaning: a device that raises a signal
items.example: The agent suffix names the thing that does the work.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀命名干这件事的物件。

items.example: The noun measures how far a wave moves.
The adjective keeps the plain sense of size.
items.exampleCN: 形容词保留「大」的平实义。

items.example: It also builds simplify, clarify and verify.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 simplify、clarify 与 verify。

definition_zh: 使发笑；逗乐；给……提供消遣
definition_en: to make someone laugh or smile, or to keep someone pleasantly occupied
core_image: 候车室里，一个孩子用纸折出小动物逗弟弟笑
scene: 长途车上，邻座的人讲了几个笑话，把整排乘客都逗笑了。The jokes amused the tired passengers.
sceneCN: 这里 amuse 是「逗乐；使发笑」（第 1 个义项：让人笑起来）；句意是这些笑话把疲惫的乘客逗乐了。

pos.zh: 动词：使发笑；逗乐；给……消遣

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有趣的；逗人笑的

senses.title: To make someone laugh
senses.definition: to cause someone to laugh or smile, usually with something funny
senses.definitionCN: 用有趣的东西让人发笑或微笑
senses.example: The jokes amused the tired passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些笑话把疲惫的乘客逗乐了。
senses.why: The word began in French with a sense of distracting or stupefying the mind, and laughter is the gentlest form of that distraction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初在法语中意为分散注意、使头脑发懵，而笑声正是这种分神最温和的形式。

senses.title: To keep pleasantly occupied
senses.definition: to give someone something enjoyable to do so that time passes happily
senses.definitionCN: 给某人有趣的事情做，使时间愉快地过去
senses.example: The museum keeps children amused for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆能让孩子们开心地待上几个小时。
senses.why: Amusement need not be laughter; anything that holds attention pleasantly keeps the mind from boredom, which is the older sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 消遣不一定要有笑声；任何能愉快地占据注意力、使心思不落到无聊上的东西都算，这正是这个词较早的含义。

intro.en: Amuse originally meant to distract the mind, not to make it laugh.
intro.cn: amuse 最初指分散心思，而不是让人发笑。

items.en: muser meant 'to stare, to ponder, to waste time', the base of the word.
items.cn: muser 意为「呆看、沉思、消磨时间」，是该词的词基。

items.en: amuser meant 'to deceive, to stupefy, to divert attention'.
items.cn: amuser 意为「欺骗、使发懵、转移注意力」。

items.en: English amuse first meant 'to divert the attention, to occupy'.
items.cn: 英语 amuse 最初意为「转移注意力、使忙碌」。

items.en: The sense narrowed towards pleasant diversion and then to making people laugh.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄为愉快的消遣，随后又指逗人发笑。

items.en: Amusing now usually means funny, while amusement covers both laughter and pastime.
items.cn: 如今 amusing 通常指好笑，而 amusement 既指笑也指消遣。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the muse base; the near-meaning group grades entertainment.
note.cn: 形近组共享 muse 词基；近义组按娱乐方式分级。

entries.definition: finding something funny
entries.definitionCN: 被逗乐的

entries.definition: funny or entertaining
entries.definitionCN: 有趣的

entries.definition: to think deeply
entries.definitionCN: 沉思

entries.definition: to amuse or interest guests
entries.definitionCN: 招待；使娱乐

entries.definition: to give great pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 使高兴

entries.definition: to take attention away
entries.definitionCN: 分散注意力

normalIntro.en: Amuse is a-muse: to lead the mind away from boredom.
normalIntro.cn: amuse 可看作 a 加 muse：把心思从无聊中引开。

normal.en: Muse means to ponder; amuse first meant to distract.
normal.cn: muse 意为沉思，amuse 最初意为分散注意。

normal.en: Amusing is the adjective for something funny.
normal.cn: amusing 是形容某物好笑的形容词。

normal.en: Be amused by, not amused from.
normal.cn: 搭配是 be amused by，不用 from。

normal.en: An amusement park is a place of pastime.
normal.cn: amusement park 是消遣之地。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-MUSE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-MUSE。

abstract.en: Picture a paper animal folded on a bus.
abstract.cn: 想象在公交车上折出的纸动物。

abstract.en: See a row of passengers smiling at a joke.
abstract.cn: 想象一排乘客被笑话逗笑。

abstract.en: Imagine a child busy for hours in a museum.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子在博物馆里玩上几个小时。

examples.en: The clown amused the children for an hour.
examples.cn: 小丑逗孩子们开心了一个小时。

examples.en: I was amused by his imitation of the teacher.
examples.cn: 他模仿老师的样子把我逗乐了。

examples.en: She amused herself by reading old letters.
examples.cn: 她读旧信来消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: a 加 muse（沉思）：把沉思的人拉出来，就是逗乐、消遣。

root: 源自古法语 amuser「欺骗、使发懵、转移注意」，其词基 muser 意为呆看、沉思；十五世纪进入英语时意为转移注意力，十七世纪渐指愉快的消遣，现代更常指逗人发笑。

sensesIntro.en: Diverting the mind yields two uses: provoking laughter and filling time pleasantly.
sensesIntro.cn: 「把心思引开」生出两种用法：引人发笑，以及愉快地打发时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded paper animal making a child smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：折纸小动物逗笑孩子。

branches.en: jokes on a long bus ride
branches.cn: 长途车上的笑话

branches.en: a clown working a crowd
branches.cn: 逗笑观众的小丑

branches.en: a museum that occupies children
branches.cn: 让孩子有事可做的博物馆

branches.en: reading old letters to pass time
branches.cn: 读旧信打发时间

branches.en: games that keep guests happy
branches.cn: 让客人开心的游戏

intro.en: A French verb with a compact English family around amusement.
intro.cn: 这是法语动词，英语中围绕 amusement 有一小族词。

latinIntro.en: The word is French rather than Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自法语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: adj. 厌氧的；无氧的；（运动）无氧的
definition_en: Living or occurring without free oxygen; of exercise, short and intense enough that the muscles work without extra oxygen.
core_image: 把氧气抽走之后，生命仍在那儿硬撑
scene: 沼气池里的细菌不需要氧气也能分解秸秆。Anaerobic bacteria break down the straw in the tank.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：沼气池是缺氧环境，里面分解秸秆的细菌属于厌氧菌，所以用 anaerobic 描述。

forms.label: 无 -er/-est 形式（多音节形容词，用 more/most）

senses.title: Life without oxygen
senses.definition: living, growing or occurring in the absence of free oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 在没有游离氧的环境中生存、生长或发生的
senses.example: Anaerobic digestion turns waste into methane.
senses.exampleCN: 厌氧消化把废弃物转化为甲烷。
senses.why: The prefix an- means without, aer is air and bios is life, so the word literally says life without air.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 an- 意为「没有」，aer 是空气，bios 是生命，所以这个词字面上说的就是「没有空气的生命」。

senses.title: Short hard exercise
senses.definition: of exercise so brief and intense that the muscles draw energy without waiting for oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 指运动短促而剧烈，肌肉不等氧气供应就取用能量
senses.example: Sprinting is anaerobic; a long jog is aerobic.
senses.exampleCN: 短跑是无氧运动，长时间慢跑是有氧运动。
senses.why: The same absence is meant, but now inside a muscle: the effort outruns the oxygen supply, so the body borrows another route.
senses.whyCN: 所指的仍是同一种「缺」，只是发生在肌肉内部：用力超过了供氧速度，身体便借用另一条路径。

intro.en: Anaerobic is Greek an-, without, plus aer, air, plus bios, life. Pasteur coined the French pair aerobie and anaerobie in the 1860s, and English took both.
intro.cn: anaerobic 由希腊语 an-「没有」加 aer「空气」加 bios「生命」构成。巴斯德在 19 世纪 60 年代造出法语的 aerobie 与 anaerobie 这一对，英语把两者都借入。

items.en: Greek an- is the form a- takes before a vowel, meaning not or without. It gives anaemia, anonymous and anarchy.
items.cn: 希腊语 an- 是 a- 在元音前的形式，意为「不、没有」。它产生 anaemia、anonymous 与 anarchy。

items.en: Greek aer meant air or mist, and gives aerial, aerate and aerodynamics.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、雾气」，产生 aerial、aerate 与 aerodynamics。

items.en: Greek bios meant life, the same piece that builds biology and amphibian.
items.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为「生命」，与构成 biology 和 amphibian 的是同一个部件。

items.en: Pasteur coined French anaerobie in the 1860s for organisms that live without free oxygen, pairing it with aerobie.
items.cn: 巴斯德在 19 世纪 60 年代造出法语 anaerobie，指无需游离氧而生活的生物，与 aerobie 配对。

items.en: English took anaerobic from that pair, and sport science later borrowed it for effort that outruns the oxygen supply.
items.cn: 英语从这一对中借入 anaerobic，运动科学后来又把它借去指超过供氧速度的用力。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the aerobe family and two an- words; the near-meaning group lists other terms for low-oxygen conditions.
note.cn: 形近组保留 aerobe 词族与两个 an- 开头的词；近义组列出其他表示低氧状态的术语。

entries.definition: Requiring free oxygen.
entries.definitionCN: 需要游离氧的。

entries.definition: An organism that lives without oxygen.
entries.definitionCN: 无需氧气而生活的生物。

entries.definition: Loss of sensation induced for surgery.
entries.definitionCN: 为手术诱导的感觉丧失。

entries.definition: Building larger molecules in the body.
entries.definitionCN: 在体内合成较大分子的。

entries.definition: Containing no oxygen at all.
entries.definitionCN: 完全不含氧的。

entries.definition: Having too little oxygen.
entries.definitionCN: 氧气过少的。

entries.definition: Describing conditions that strip oxygen away.
entries.definitionCN: 描述夺走氧气的条件。

normalIntro.en: Anaerobic is an- plus aer plus bic: no air, so life that runs without oxygen.
normalIntro.cn: anaerobic 就是 an- 加 aer 加 bic：没有空气，所以是不靠氧气运行的生命。

normal.en: Drop the an- and you get aerobic, the exact opposite.
normal.cn: 去掉 an- 就得到 aerobic，正好相反。

normal.en: Anaerobic digestion makes methane; aerobic composting makes heat.
normal.cn: 厌氧消化产甲烷，好氧堆肥产热。

normal.en: Sprinting and lifting are anaerobic; jogging is aerobic.
normal.cn: 短跑与举重是无氧的，慢跑是有氧的。

normal.en: The noun for the organism is an anaerobe.
normal.cn: 指该生物的名词是 anaerobe。

normal.en: Do not confuse anaerobic with anabolic, which is about building tissue.
normal.cn: 别把 anaerobic 与 anabolic 混淆，后者讲合成组织。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed tank bubbling without any air.
abstract.cn: 想象一只密闭罐子在毫无空气的情况下冒泡。

abstract.en: Imagine a sprinter finishing before the lungs catch up.
abstract.cn: 想象短跑者在肺还没跟上时就已冲线。

abstract.en: Think of mud at the bottom of a pond, black and airless.
abstract.cn: 想象池底的黑泥，没有一丝空气。

examples.en: Anaerobic bacteria thrive deep in the sediment.
examples.cn: 厌氧菌在沉积物深处繁盛。

examples.en: The treatment plant uses anaerobic digestion to cut sludge.
examples.cn: 处理厂用厌氧消化来减少污泥。

examples.en: Heavy lifting is largely anaerobic work.
examples.cn: 大重量举重主要是无氧做功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「无」+ aero「空气」+ bic「生命」——没有空气也能活，就是厌氧的；短跑喘不上气那一段也是无氧的。

root: 希腊语 an-「无」+ aer「空气」+ bios「生命」，由巴斯德造出法语 anaerobie，英语加 -ic 成 anaerobic，字面即「无空气而生活的」，引申指无氧运动。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one absence of oxygen: in a sealed tank of bacteria, and in a muscle working faster than the lungs can supply.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种「缺氧」：一是在密闭的细菌罐里，二是在供氧跟不上的肌肉里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life keeping going after the oxygen is pulled out
core.cn: 核心意象：氧气被抽走后生命仍在硬撑

branches.en: Black mud bubbling with methane.
branches.cn: 冒着甲烷气泡的黑泥。

branches.en: A sealed digester turning waste to gas.
branches.cn: 把废弃物变成气体的密闭消化罐。

branches.en: A forty-metre dash run on stored fuel.
branches.cn: 靠储备燃料跑完的四十米冲刺。

branches.en: A last heavy lift with held breath.
branches.cn: 憋着气完成的最后一次大重量举。

branches.en: Both run without waiting for oxygen.
branches.cn: 两者都不等氧气就运行。

intro.en: Anaerobic is an- plus aer plus bio plus -ic, and removing the prefix flips the whole meaning.
intro.cn: anaerobic 是 an- 加 aer 加 bio 加 -ic，去掉前缀就把整个意思翻过来。

latinIntro.en: All three pieces are Greek: an-, aer and bios. Pasteur assembled them in French, and English only added the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 三个部件全是希腊语：an-、aer 与 bios。巴斯德在法语中把它们组装起来，英语只加了形容词词尾。

latinEntries.exampleCN: aer 产生 aerobic 与 aerial。
bios 产生 biology 与 anaerobe。

definition_zh: 可类比的；相似的；同功的；类推的
definition_en: similar in a way that permits a comparison between two different things, especially in structure or function
core_image: 两副骨架并排摆在展台上，一副来自鸟，一副来自飞机，翼形与受力路径一一对应，材料却完全不同
scene: 博物馆展台上并排摆着鸟翼与机翼的剖面，骨架与梁架一一对应，材料却各不相同。A bird's wing is analogous to an aircraft wing in function.
sceneCN: 这里指两种不同事物之间存在可对照的结构关系（第 1 个义项：跨域可类比）；句意为鸟翼在功能上与飞机机翼可以类比。图中可辨识物件：鸟翼剖面、机翼剖面、对应的骨架与梁架。

pos.zh: 可类比的；相似的；同功的；类推的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词同族的名词形式，义为「类比；相似」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「类似地；可类比地」
经法语而来的同族名词，义为「相似物；模拟量」
美式拼写的同族形容词，义为「模拟的」

senses.title: Comparable across different domains
senses.definition: able to be compared with something from another field because both answer to the same measure
senses.definitionCN: 因两者符合同一尺度，可以与另一领域的某物相比较
senses.example: The two economies are analogous in their reliance on exports.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个经济体在依赖出口这一点上可以类比。
senses.why: The Greek adjective meant proportionate, so the earliest comparison was between things measured on one scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊形容词意为成比例的，因此最早的比较是在同一尺度上衡量两物。

senses.title: Similar in function but not in origin
senses.definition: describing body parts that perform the same job without sharing an evolutionary origin
senses.definitionCN: 指承担相同功能却并非来自同一演化来源的身体结构
senses.example: A bat's wing is analogous to a bird's wing, though their bones differ.
senses.exampleCN: 蝙蝠的翼与鸟的翼是同功结构，尽管骨骼并不相同。
senses.why: Biology needed a word for matching jobs, leaving the matching ancestry to the word homologous.
senses.whyCN: 生物学需要一个表示「功能相同」的词，而把「来源相同」留给同源这个词。

senses.title: Reasoning by comparison
senses.definition: reaching a conclusion about one case by comparing it with a known similar case
senses.definitionCN: 通过与已知的类似情形比较，得出关于另一情形的结论
senses.example: The engineer used an analogous line of reasoning to test the new design.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用一条类比推理的思路来检验新设计。
senses.why: If two things answer to one ratio, a step that works for the first can be carried over to the second.
senses.whyCN: 如果两物符合同一比例，对前者有效的一步就可以搬到后者身上。

senses.title: Reasoning across legal cases
senses.definition: applying a rule from one decided case to another case that is not identical but comparable
senses.definitionCN: 把已决案例中的规则用到另一个不完全相同但可比的情形上
senses.example: Lawyers applied an analogous rule from an earlier case.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们援引了早先案例中一条类似的规则。
senses.why: Law rests on precedent, and precedent works only if the new case can be matched to the old one.
senses.whyCN: 法律依靠先例，而先例只有在新案件能与旧案件对应时才起作用。

senses.title: Matching in function
senses.definition: serving the same purpose in two different systems, whatever the materials or shapes involved
senses.definitionCN: 在两个不同系统中承担相同的用途，不论材料或形状如何
senses.example: The two valves are analogous in function but not in shape.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个阀门在功能上相对应，形状却不同。
senses.why: Function is the measure here: if the job is the same, the parts can be called analogous.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尺度是功能：只要承担的任务相同，这些部件就可以称为对应。

senses.title: The fixed phrase with to
senses.definition: used in the pattern be analogous to, naming the second term of the comparison
senses.definitionCN: 用于「be analogous to」这一句式，引出比较的另一方
senses.example: Her role in the firm is analogous to that of a coach.
senses.exampleCN: 她在公司里的角色相当于一名教练。
senses.why: The preposition to marks the direction of the comparison, and the phrase has become a fixed frame.
senses.whyCN: 介词「to」标出比较的方向，这个短语因而成了固定框架。

senses.title: A likeness drawn for persuasion
senses.definition: a comparison used in speech or writing to make an abstract idea vivid rather than to prove a point
senses.definitionCN: 在言语或写作中用比较使抽象概念生动，而不是为了证明论点
senses.example: The poem draws an analogous image between a river and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗在河流与记忆之间画出一幅可类比的意象。
senses.why: Rhetoric borrows the word for comparisons that persuade by resemblance, even when no proof is offered.
senses.whyCN: 修辞学借这个词指靠相似来说服的比较，即使并不提供证明。

senses.title: Correspondence between whole systems
senses.definition: a pattern in which two separate systems mirror each other in their arrangement or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 两个独立系统在结构或行为上彼此映照的模式
senses.example: The two networks show analogous patterns of connection.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个网络显示出可类比的连接模式。
senses.why: Once the comparison is between whole systems, the word describes a shared architecture rather than single parts.
senses.whyCN: 当比较发生在整个系统之间，这个词描述的是共有的架构，而非单个部件。

intro.en: Analogous comes from Greek analogos, proportionate or corresponding, built from ana-, according to, and logos, ratio, reason or word; it entered English through Latin analogus.
intro.cn: 这个词来自希腊语「analogos」成比例的、相应的，由「ana-」按照与「logos」比例、道理、言词构成；经拉丁语「analogus」进入英语。

items.en: The prefix means according to or in proportion, and it sets the frame of a shared measure.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为按照或成比例，它给出共同尺度的框架。

items.en: Logos covered ratio, proportion, reason and word, so the comparison was always rational as well as verbal.
items.cn: 这个词涵盖比例、道理、言词，因此这种比较既是言辞的，也是理性的。

items.en: The adjective meant proportionate or corresponding, said of things that answer to the same measure.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为成比例的、相应的，用于符合同一尺度的事物。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective unchanged in meaning and passed it on to English.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词，意义不变，再传给英语。

items.en: English took the adjective in the sixteenth century and formed the noun analogy beside it.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入这个形容词，并在旁边造出名词「analogy」。

items.en: Biology applied it to structures with the same function but a different origin, and law to reasoning across cases.
items.cn: 生物学用它指功能相同而来源不同的结构，法律用它指跨案例的推理。

note.en: The first group looks like analogous or shares its Greek stem, including analogue and analog; the second group names nearby ideas of likeness. Note that similar merely says two things resemble each other, while analogous claims a correspondence of structure or function across different fields.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「analogous」相近或共享希腊词干，包含「analogue」与「analog」；第二组是与「相似」相邻的说法。要注意「similar」只泛指相像，而「analogous」强调跨领域在结构或功能上的对应。

entries.definition: A comparison that sets two things side by side to show a shared pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 指把两事物并置以显示共同模式的比较。

entries.definition: A thing that corresponds to another, or a signal that varies continuously.
entries.definitionCN: 指与另一物相对应之物，也指连续变化的模拟信号。

entries.definition: The American spelling of analogue, used especially for continuous signals and clocks.
entries.definitionCN: 「analogue」的美式拼写，尤用于连续信号与钟表。

entries.definition: Adjective for reasoning by comparison rather than by deduction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容以比较而非演绎进行的推理。

entries.definition: Open to more than one reading; it looks close but comes from a verb meaning to wander, not from logos.
entries.definitionCN: 指可有多种解释的；形近但出自意为游移的动词，与「logos」无关。

entries.definition: Resembling another thing in appearance or nature, without claiming any structural match.
entries.definitionCN: 指在外观或性质上相像，并不声称结构上的对应。

entries.definition: Able to be measured or judged against another on the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以在同一尺度上与另一物衡量或比较。

entries.definition: Running alongside and matching in pattern, often of lines, trends or lives.
entries.definitionCN: 指并行且在模式上对应，常用于线路、趋势或人生。

entries.definition: Equal in value, force or meaning rather than merely similar in form.
entries.definitionCN: 指在价值、效力或意义上相等，而不只是形式上相像。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek measure behind the word, its real family and the fields where the term is standard.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后的希腊尺度、真实同族词，以及这个词常用的领域。

normal.en: Greek logos is ratio, so analogous things answer to the same measure even when they are made of different stuff.
normal.cn: 希腊语「logos」是比例，因此可类比之物即使材料不同，也符合同一尺度。

normal.en: An analogy, an analogue and an analog all keep the idea of one thing answering to another.
normal.cn: 类比、相似物与模拟量都保留着「一物对应另一物」的意思。

normal.en: Biology calls a bat's wing analogous to a bird's wing because both fly, not because they share ancestors.
normal.cn: 生物学称蝙蝠翼与鸟翼同功，是因为两者都会飞，而不是因为共有祖先。

normal.en: Lawyers speak of an analogous case when an old rule can be stretched to a new situation.
normal.cn: 当旧规则可以延伸到新情形时，律师会说这是一个类似案例。

normal.en: Analogous to is the fixed phrase, and it always wants the second term after to.
normal.cn: 「analogous to」是固定搭配，后面总要跟比较的另一方。

abstract.en: Similarity of shape is easy to see; correspondence of function is what analogous asks you to prove.
abstract.cn: 形状相像容易看见，功能对应才是「analogous」要你证明的东西。

abstract.en: Two things made of different materials can still answer to one ratio, and that is the quiet claim of the word.
abstract.cn: 材料不同的两样东西仍可符合同一比例，这正是这个词低调的主张。

abstract.en: An analogy is a bridge built from a known bank to an unknown one, and it must be tested before it is trusted.
abstract.cn: 类比是一座从已知岸搭向未知岸的桥，信任它之前必须先检验。

examples.en: The heart's pumping action is analogous to a mechanical pump.
examples.cn: 心脏的泵血作用类似于一台机械泵。

examples.en: An analogous problem appeared in the earlier design of the bridge.
examples.cn: 这座桥早先的设计中也出现过类似的问题。

examples.en: Biologists treat these two organs as analogous rather than homologous.
examples.cn: 生物学家把这两个器官视为同功结构，而不是同源结构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿那勒格斯」——两样东西材料不同、骨架却对得上，可以横着比一比：可类比的、同功的

root: 希腊语「analogos」意为成比例的、相应的，由「ana-」按照加「logos」比例、道理、言词构成；经拉丁语「analogus」进入英语。它与泛指相像的「similar」不同，强调跨领域在结构或功能上的对应。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one idea of correspondence: across fields, in biology, in reasoning, in law, in function, in the fixed phrase, in rhetoric, and between whole systems.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个「对应」的念头：跨领域、生物学、推理、法律、功能、固定搭配、修辞，以及整个系统之间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird's wing and an aircraft wing lie side by side, bone for strut, with different materials and the same job.
core.cn: 核心意象：鸟翼与机翼并排摆放，骨骼对梁架，材料不同而功用相同。

branches.en: THE GENERAL COMPARISON: two separate domains are placed on one measure, and reasoning follows.
branches.cn: 一般比较：两个不同领域被放在同一尺度上，推理随之展开。

branches.en: THE MATCHED ORGAN: biology and engineering judge by function rather than by origin.
branches.cn: 对应的器官：生物学与工程学按功能而非来源来判断。

branches.en: THE BORROWED RULE AND THE FIXED FRAME: a rule crosses cases, and the phrase takes to.
branches.cn: 借来的规则与固定框架：规则跨案例使用，而短语以「to」引出对象。

branches.en: THE RHETORICAL FIGURE: a likeness is drawn to persuade, not to prove.
branches.cn: 修辞手法：画出相似是为了说服，而不是为了证明。

branches.en: THE PAIRED SYSTEMS: whole networks answer to each other's patterns.
branches.cn: 成对的系统：整个网络彼此呼应对方的模式。

intro.en: Analogous is a Greek adjective built from a prefix of proportion and a noun of ratio, and English keeps the family together.
intro.cn: 这是一个由表示比例的前缀与表示比例的名词构成的希腊形容词，英语把这一族词保留在一起。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies analogos and its parts, and Latin supplies analogia and analogus before English takes them over.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了「analogos」及其组成部分，拉丁语又提供「analogia」与「analogus」，再由英语接手。

items.example: The adjective is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The prefix sets the shared measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀设定共同的尺度。

items.example: The noun supplies the measuring half.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「尺度」那一半。

items.example: The noun names the relation itself.
Latin passed the adjective to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词传给英语。

items.example: The word keeps the idea of a matched counterpart.
items.exampleCN: 这个词保留「对应物」的意思。

derivatives.zh: 由同一希腊词干构成的名词，义为「类比；相似」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「类似地」
经法语而来的同族名词，义为「相似物；模拟量」
美式拼写的同族形容词，义为「模拟的」

definition_zh: 类比；类推；比喻
definition_en: a comparison between two things that shows how they are similar in some way
core_image: 用熟悉的地图解释陌生的城市
scene: 老师用电厂水流解释电流的原理。The teacher drew an analogy between flowing water and electric current.
sceneCN: 这里的 analogy 是「类比」（第 1 个义项：两物的相似性比较）；句意是老师在流水与电流之间作类比讲解。

collocations.phrase: the argument rests on an analogy

derivatives.zh: 由 analogy 的词根 analog- 派生，义为「类似的、可类比的」
同根词，义为「模拟的（连续信号）」，与数字 digital 相对
由 analog- 加 -ize 构成，义为「作类比推理」
同根名词，义为「相似物；对应物」

senses.title: A comparison of similarities
senses.definition: a comparison made to explain one thing by pointing out how it resembles another, usually a familiar one
senses.definitionCN: 借助两物的相似性，尤其用熟悉的事物来解释陌生的事物
senses.example: She used an analogy of a bathtub to explain supply and demand.
senses.exampleCN: 她用浴缸作类比来解释供需关系。
senses.why: Ana- means according to and logos means ratio or reckoning; an analogy lays things side by side in the same ratio.
senses.whyCN: ana- 表示「按照」，logos 表示「比例、推理」；类比就是按同一比例把两物并排摆好。

senses.title: Reasoning from parallel cases
senses.definition: a form of reasoning that concludes something about one case because it resembles another case
senses.definitionCN: 因两案相似而由一案推及另一案的推理方式
senses.example: By analogy with earlier rulings, the court allowed the appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 参照先例类推，法院受理了上诉。
senses.why: The same ratio that explains can also argue: if two things match in known parts, they may match in the unknown part.
senses.whyCN: 同一比例既能解释也能论证：已知部分相合，未知部分也可推定相合。

senses.title: Partial likeness between things
senses.definition: an actual point of resemblance between two things, not just the act of comparing
senses.definitionCN: 两物之间实际存在的相似点，而非比较这一行为
senses.example: There is a close analogy between bird wings and whale flippers.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟翼与鲸鳍之间存在明显的同源相似。
senses.why: Once comparison is possible, the similarity it reveals can be named by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然可以比较，比较所揭示的相似本身也用这个词来命名。

intro.en: Analogy comes from Greek analogia, proportion, from ana according to plus logos ratio.
intro.cn: analogy 源自希腊语 analogia「比例」，由 ana（按照）+ logos（比例、推理）构成。

items.en: The root *leg- behind logos meant to gather or to pick out words.
items.cn: logos 背后的词根 *leg- 表示「收集、选取词语」。

items.en: Greek analogia meant proportion, as in the equality of ratios in mathematics.
items.cn: 希腊语 analogia 意为「比例」，用于数学中比率相等之义。

items.en: Latin analogia kept the mathematical and rhetorical senses.
items.cn: 拉丁语 analogia 保留了数学与修辞两方面的意义。

items.en: French analogie passed the word into scholarly usage.
items.cn: 法语 analogie 使该词进入学术用语。

items.en: English adopted analogy in the 16th century for proportion, then for likeness and reasoning from likeness.
items.cn: 英语 16 世纪借入 analogy，先指比例，后指相似性与由相似而作的推理。

note.en: Analogy belongs to the log- word family and is contrasted with metaphor and literal statement.
note.cn: analogy 属 log- 词族，与 metaphor 及直陈说法相对。

entries.definition: similar in a way that allows comparison
entries.definitionCN: 类似的、可类比的，analogy 的形容词

entries.definition: a thing corresponding to another
entries.definitionCN: 对应物；模拟的，同根名词与形容词

entries.definition: an expression of regret
entries.definitionCN: 道歉，与 analogy 拼写相近但词根不同（apo- 离开）

entries.definition: the study of living things
entries.definitionCN: 生物学，同用 -logy（学、论说）词尾

entries.definition: the act of examining similarities and differences
entries.definitionCN: 比较，比 analogy 更中性、更全面

entries.definition: a figure of speech naming one thing as another
entries.definitionCN: 隐喻，直接把甲说成乙，而 analogy 是摆出相似关系

entries.definition: a close similarity between two things
entries.definitionCN: 相似之处、平行例证

entries.definition: a match between things
entries.definitionCN: 对应关系

entries.definition: plain direct wording without comparison
entries.definitionCN: 直陈表述，与类比修辞相对

normalIntro.en: Hold ana- plus logos, ratio, to fix analogy in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 抓住 ana- 加 logos（比例）来记 analogy。

normal.en: ana- means according to; logos means ratio or word.
normal.cn: ana- 表示「按照」；logos 表示「比例、言语」。

normal.en: the plural changes y to ies: analogies.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 ies：analogies。

normal.en: draw an analogy between is the key phrase.
normal.cn: 关键搭配是 draw an analogy between。

normal.en: analogous is the adjective partner.
normal.cn: 形容词搭档是 analogous。

normal.en: analogy argues, metaphor paints.
normal.cn: 类比用来论证，隐喻用来描绘。

abstract.en: See a teacher holding a map beside an unfamiliar city plan.
abstract.cn: 想象老师把熟悉的城市地图摆在陌生蓝图旁对照。

abstract.en: Picture two unequal beams balanced by a moving weight.
abstract.cn: 想象两根不等长杠杆被砝码调平，比例即类比的骨架。

abstract.en: Feel two unfamiliar roads easing your path once they echo one another.
abstract.cn: 感受两条相似道路彼此呼应、让路途变熟。

examples.en: He drew an analogy between the immune system and an army.
examples.cn: 他把免疫系统类比为一支军队。

examples.en: By analogy, the same rule should govern both cases.
examples.cn: 依此类推，同一规则应适用于两案。

examples.en: The analogy is helpful, though not exact.
examples.cn: 这个类比虽有助理解，但并不完全贴切。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺那老记」——俺那老记性不好，就用熟悉的例子打比方：一比就懂，这就是 analogy（类比）。

root: 希腊语 ana-（按照、相对）+ logos（比例；言语）+ -ia（名词后缀），analogia 本义「成比例」。同族词 analogous、analogue、analogize。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from the explanatory comparison, through reasoning by parallel cases, to the likeness itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从「解释性的比较」出发，经「依据相似案例的类推」，最终落在「相似性本身」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the known laid beside the unknown in the same ratio
core.cn: 核心意象：把已知与未知按同一比例并排放置

branches.en: Explaining the strange through the familiar
branches.cn: 以熟释生，即类比说明

branches.en: The same likeness used to argue
branches.cn: 同一相似性转作论证之用

branches.en: Reasoning across parallel cases
branches.cn: 在平行案例间推理，即类推

branches.en: The conclusion resting on the resemblance found
branches.cn: 结论立足于所找到的相似点

branches.en: Resemblance as a fact of structure
branches.cn: 相似性作为结构事实，如鸟翼与鲸鳍

intro.en: Analogy builds on ana- and the great root logos.

senses.title: To examine in detail
senses.definition: to study something closely by separating it into its parts in order to understand it
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物拆成若干部分仔细研究，以求理解
senses.example: Researchers analysed the data from ten thousand households.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员分析了一万个家庭的数据。
senses.why: The Greek verb behind the word meant 'to loosen up', so to analyse is to loosen a whole into its parts until the structure shows.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的希腊动词意为「解开」，所以 analyse 就是把整体拆松成部分，直到结构显露出来。

senses.title: To test a substance
senses.definition: to break a substance down chemically in order to identify what it contains
senses.definitionCN: 用化学方法把物质分解，以确定其成分
senses.example: The lab analysed the water samples for traces of lead.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室检测了水样中是否含铅。
senses.why: Chemistry took the 'loosening into parts' literally, so analyse can mean dissolving a sample into measurable components.
senses.whyCN: 化学把这个「拆成部分」的动作照字面使用，所以 analyse 可以指把样本分解成可测量的成分。

senses.title: To treat by psychoanalysis
senses.definition: to treat a patient by exploring unconscious thoughts and feelings
senses.definitionCN: 通过探究无意识的思想与情感来治疗病人
senses.example: The patient was analysed by a Freudian therapist for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人接受了一位弗洛伊德派治疗师两年的精神分析。
senses.why: Psychoanalysis borrowed the word because it takes a mind apart into hidden drives, the same loosening applied to the psyche.
senses.whyCN: 精神分析借用这个词，是因为它把心灵拆解为隐藏的驱力，是同一套「拆松」用在心理层面。

intro.en: Analyse carries a Greek verb meaning to loosen, which is why analysis feels like taking something apart.

items.cn: 前缀 ana- 意为「向上、贯穿」，带来彻底性的意味。

items.en: lyein meant 'to loosen, to untie', the core of the word.
items.cn: lyein 意为「松开、解开」，是这个词的核心。

items.en: analyein meant 'to loosen up, to dissolve', used of both objects and arguments.
items.cn: analyein 意为「解开、分解」，既用于物体也用于论证。

items.en: The noun analysis passed into Latin and then into the modern languages.
items.cn: 名词 analysis 传入拉丁语，再进入现代各语言。

items.en: French formed the verb analyser, which English borrowed as analyse.
items.cn: 法语构成动词 analyser，英语借入为 analyse。

senses.why: Freud's method takes the mind apart in the same way, so English uses the bare noun analysis for the treatment itself.
senses.whyCN: 弗洛伊德的方法也是以同样方式拆解心灵，因此英语直接用 analysis 这个词指这种治疗。

definition_zh: n. 无政府主义（主张废除国家与强制性等级）
definition_en: The political belief that the state and all coercive hierarchy should be abolished and society organised through voluntary cooperation.
core_image: 把头顶那把椅子搬走，人们自己围成一圈
scene: 这本小册子主张用合作社取代官僚机构。Anarchism shaped the early labour movement here.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：小册子主张废除强制性的国家机构，由自愿合作来组织社会，这就是 anarchism 的核心主张。

senses.title: The political doctrine
senses.definition: the belief that coercive government should be replaced by voluntary associations and mutual aid
senses.definitionCN: 主张以自愿结社与互助取代强制性政府的信念
senses.example: Anarchism argues that order need not come from above.
senses.exampleCN: 无政府主义主张秩序不必自上而下产生。
senses.why: Greek an- means without and arkhos means ruler, so the word names a programme of doing without rulers, not a programme of chaos.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 an- 意为「没有」，arkhos 意为「统治者」，所以这个词命名的是一套「不要统治者」的方案，而不是「要混乱」的方案。

senses.title: The historical movement
senses.titleCN: 历史上的无政府主义运动
senses.definition: the body of thought, writers and organisations that carried that doctrine from the nineteenth century onward
senses.definitionCN: 自 19 世纪起承载该学说的思想、作者与组织的总体
senses.example: Spanish anarchism drew millions of workers before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战前西班牙的无政府主义运动吸引了数百万工人。
senses.why: Once the doctrine had newspapers, unions and congresses, the same word came to name a movement with a history rather than only an idea.
senses.whyCN: 当这套学说有了报纸、工会与代表大会，同一个词便转而指一场有历史的运动，而不只是一个想法。

intro.en: Anarchism is Greek an-, without, plus arkhos, ruler, plus -ism. Proudhon made French anarchisme a positive programme in 1840, turning an old word for disorder into a doctrine.
intro.cn: anarchism 由希腊语 an-「没有」加 arkhos「统治者」加 -ism 构成。蒲鲁东在 1840 年把法语 anarchisme 变成一套正面方案，把一个原指混乱的旧词变成了学说。

items.en: Greek an- means not or without before a vowel, the same prefix that builds anaerobic and anonymous.
items.cn: 希腊语 an- 在元音前意为「不、没有」，与构成 anaerobic 和 anonymous 的是同一前缀。

items.en: Greek arkhos meant leader or ruler, from arkhein, to begin or to rule. It gives monarchy, oligarchy and hierarchy.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhos 意为「首领、统治者」，来自 arkhein「开始、统治」。它产生 monarchy、oligarchy 与 hierarchy。

items.en: Greek anarkhia meant the absence of a ruler, and in Athens it described a year without a chief magistrate, usually with disapproval.
items.cn: 希腊语 anarkhia 意为「没有统治者」，在雅典指没有首席执政官的年份，通常带贬义。

items.en: Proudhon declared himself an anarchist in 1840 and used French anarchisme for a positive order built on contracts and mutual credit.
items.cn: 蒲鲁东在 1840 年自称无政府主义者，并用法语 anarchisme 指建立在契约与互助信贷之上的正面秩序。

items.en: English took anarchism in the mid nineteenth century, and the word now covers both the doctrine and the movements that carried it.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪中期借入 anarchism，如今该词既指学说，也指承载它的各场运动。

note.cn: 形近组把 anarchism 与意为「混乱」的 anarchy 分开；近义组列出相邻的政治思潮。

core_image: 一具被细心分层的躯干示意图，肌肉、血管与骨骼逐层揭开
scene: 医学院的新生第一学期就要背骨头。Anatomy students spend the first term learning every bone of the hand.
sceneCN: 这里 anatomy 指「解剖学」（第 1 个义项：研究生物体结构的学科）；句意：解剖学学生第一学期要学完手部每一块骨头。图中可辨识物件：分层人体图、手部骨骼标本、标注签。

pos.zh: 解剖学；身体结构；解剖（行为）；剖析（可数时指某生物或某系统的结构）

derivatives.zh: 原子（同出希腊 temnein「切」，但前缀相反，见 similar）

senses.title: The Science of Structure
senses.titleCN: 解剖学：研究身体结构的学科
senses.definition: the scientific study of the structure of living bodies
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物体结构的科学
senses.example: Anatomy students spend the first term learning every bone of the hand.
senses.exampleCN: 解剖学学生第一学期要学完手部每一块骨头。
senses.why: Greek ana- meant 'up, throughout' and temnein meant 'to cut'. Anatomē was a cutting-up, and the name of the act became the name of the science that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊前缀 ana- 意为「向上、遍及」，temnein 意为「切」。anatomē 就是「切开」，这个动作的名称后来变成了从事该动作的学科名称。

senses.title: Body Structure Itself
senses.titleCN: 身体结构：部件如何安排
senses.definition: the actual structure of a body, its parts and their arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 身体实际的结构、各部分及其排列
senses.example: The dolphin's anatomy shows that its flipper is a modified arm.
senses.exampleCN: 海豚的身体结构表明，它的鳍肢是改造过的手臂。
senses.why: The same noun names the object as well as the study. When a biologist says 'the anatomy of the dolphin', the cutting has become a description of what was found.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指学科也指对象；当生物学家说 the anatomy of the dolphin 时，「切」已经变成了对所见之物的描述。

senses.title: The Act of Dissection
senses.titleCN: 解剖：切开并分离的动作
senses.definition: the act or practice of cutting a body apart to study it
senses.definitionCN: 为研究而把身体切开的动作或做法
senses.example: The anatomy of the specimen took the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 对这份标本的解剖花了一整个下午。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the physical cutting. Modern laboratories may use imaging instead, but the word still remembers the knife.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：实际的切割。现代实验室可能改用成像技术，但这个词仍记得那把刀。

senses.title: Detailed Analysis
senses.titleCN: 剖析：把一个整体拆开来看
senses.definition: a detailed examination of the parts of a thing or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对事物或观念的各个部分所作的细致检查
senses.example: The book is an anatomy of how rumours spread.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是对谣言如何传播的一次剖析。
senses.why: The metaphor is exact: to understand a whole, take it apart part by part. Analysts therefore borrow the anatomist's word for structures that are not biological.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻非常贴切：要理解一个整体，就把它一部分一部分拆开。因此分析者借解剖学家的词，用于并非生物的结构。

senses.title: The Human Body
senses.definition: the human body, especially in informal or humorous use
senses.definitionCN: 人的身体，尤用于口语或戏谑
senses.example: He fell and bruised his entire anatomy.
senses.exampleCN: 他摔了一跤，全身都碰伤了。
senses.why: Because anatomy studies the body, the noun can stand for the body itself. The tone is usually light, as if the speaker were looking at the body from outside.
senses.whyCN: 因为解剖学研究身体，这个名词可以代指身体本身；语气通常轻松，仿佛说话者从外部打量这具身体。

senses.title: Plant and Animal Structure
senses.titleCN: 动植物结构：非人体的解剖
senses.definition: the structure of plants or animals studied as a field
senses.definitionCN: 作为研究领域的植物或动物结构
senses.example: Plant anatomy explains why stems bend toward light.
senses.exampleCN: 植物解剖学解释了茎为何向光弯曲。
senses.why: The science is not limited to people. Comparative anatomy compares species, and plant anatomy studies tissues; the same cutting-up logic applies.
senses.whyCN: 这门科学并不限于人。比较解剖学比较各物种，植物解剖学研究组织；「切开来看」的逻辑是一样的。

senses.title: Structure of an Institution
senses.titleCN: 机构的结构：组织如何构成
senses.definition: the internal structure and working parts of an organization or system
senses.definitionCN: 组织或系统的内部结构与运作部件
senses.example: The report examined the anatomy of the health service.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告考察了医疗服务体系的结构。
senses.why: Institutions have parts that can be mapped like organs. The word implies that the parts are interdependent, so a change in one shows up elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 机构有可以像器官一样被描绘的部件；这个词暗示各部件相互依赖，因此改一处就会在别处显现。

senses.title: The Anatomy Course
senses.titleCN: 解剖学课程：作为科目的解剖
senses.definition: the subject or course taught under this name
senses.definitionCN: 以解剖学为名讲授的科目或课程
senses.example: She passed anatomy but failed physiology.
senses.exampleCN: 她解剖学通过了，生理学却没过。
senses.why: In medical schools the science becomes a subject with exams. Names of disciplines often work this way: biology is both a field and a class at nine o'clock.
senses.whyCN: 在医学院，这门科学变成有考试的科目。学科名称常如此运作：biology 既是研究领域，也是九点钟的那堂课。

intro.en: Anatomy comes from Greek anatomē 'a cutting up', from ana- 'up, throughout' and temnein 'to cut'. Latin borrowed it as anatomia, and English took it in the sixteenth century; the exact date is approximate.
intro.cn: anatomy 出自希腊 anatomē「切开」，由 ana-「向上、遍及」与 temnein「切」构成。拉丁语借作 anatomia，英语于十六世纪引入；确切年代为约数。

items.en: Temnein meant 'to cut'. From it came tomos 'a cut' and the adjective -tomos, which survives in English compounds such as appendectomy and lobotomy.
items.cn: temnein 意为「切」，由此产生 tomos「切口」与形容词 -tomos；后者在英语复合词中留存，如 appendectomy（阑尾切除术）、lobotomy（脑叶切断术）。

items.en: The same root produced atomos, 'uncuttable', from a- 'not' plus tomos. Democritus used it for the smallest indivisible piece of matter. Anatomy and atom are therefore opposites built from one verb: one cuts up, the other cannot be cut.
items.cn: 同一词根产生 atomos「不可切的」，由 a-「不」加 tomos 构成；德谟克利特用它指不可再分的最小物质。因此 anatomy 与 atom 是由同一个动词造出的反义对：一个切开，一个不可切。

items.en: Anatomē meant 'a cutting up, dissection'. Greek medicine used it for the procedure of opening a body to learn its parts, not for the parts themselves.
items.cn: anatomē 意为「切开、解剖」。希腊医学用它指打开身体以了解其部件的操作，而不是指部件本身。

items.en: Latin anatomia kept both the act and the science. Medieval and Renaissance anatomists added the sense 'the structure so revealed', which English inherited.
items.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 同时保留行为与学科两义；中世纪与文艺复兴时期的解剖学家又添上「由此揭示的结构」这一含义，英语继承了它。

items.en: From the seventeenth century English extended anatomy to the parts of anything, from a poem to a government. The metaphor survives because every whole can be taken apart.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，英语把 anatomy 扩展到任何事物的部件，从一首诗到一个政府。这个比喻之所以存活，是因为任何整体都可以拆开。

note.en: The first group separates members of the Greek cutting family that look alike. The second holds near-synonyms for study, body and analysis.
note.cn: 第一组区分希腊「切」词族中形近的成员；第二组是表示研究、身体与分析的近义词。

entries.definition: The smallest unit of an element, named by Greek atomos 'uncuttable'. It is the exact opposite prefix to anatomy, which is about cutting up.
entries.definitionCN: 元素的最小单位，名称来自希腊 atomos「不可切的」；它的前缀恰与 anatomy「切开」相反。

entries.definition: Relating to anatomy or to body structure. It modifies nouns such as structure, position and model.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指与解剖学或身体结构有关的；修饰 structure、position、model 等名词。

entries.definition: A person who studies or practises anatomy. It names the human agent, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或从事解剖的人；命名的是人，而非领域。

entries.definition: The act of cutting something apart for study. It is the procedure, while anatomy can also be the science or the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 为研究而切开某物的行为；它是操作过程，而 anatomy 还可指学科或结构。

entries.definition: The study of how body parts work. Anatomy asks what the parts are; physiology asks what they do.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体部件如何运作的学科；anatomy 问部件是什么，physiology 问它们做什么。

entries.definition: The study of form, especially in biology and linguistics. It is broader than anatomy and does not imply dissection.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形式的学科，尤用于生物学与语言学；比 anatomy 更宽，且不暗示解剖。

entries.definition: The way parts are put together. It is the neutral word; anatomy adds the biological or systematic flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分的组合方式；是中性词，而 anatomy 增添了生物学或系统性的色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ana- 'up, throughout' + temnein 'cut' + -y: the cutting-up that reveals structure.
normal.cn: ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」+ -y：揭示结构的切开。

normal.en: The family runs anatomical, anatomically, anatomist, anatomize, and the -tomy words such as appendectomy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize，以及 appendectomy 一类 -tomy 词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: human anatomy, comparative anatomy, plant anatomy, gross anatomy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：人体解剖学、比较解剖学、植物解剖学、大体解剖学。

normal.en: atom is the same root with the opposite prefix: 'not cuttable' against 'cut up'.
normal.cn: atom 是同一词根加相反前缀：不可切，对比切开。

normal.en: anatomy asks what the parts are; physiology asks what they do.
normal.cn: anatomy 问部件是什么，physiology 问部件做什么。

abstract.en: Picture a watch opened on a table, every wheel laid out in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表在桌上被打开，每个齿轮都按顺序摆好。

abstract.en: Picture a map of a city printed as layers: roads, pipes, then power lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市地图分层印出：先是道路，再是管道，然后是电线。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence taken apart word by word to see how it holds together.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子被逐词拆开，以看清它如何组合。

examples.en: Human anatomy has changed little since the Renaissance.
examples.cn: 自文艺复兴以来，人体解剖学变化不大。

examples.en: The anatomy of a frog is often taught before that of a mammal.
examples.cn: 教学上常先讲青蛙的解剖结构，再讲哺乳动物。

examples.en: Her paper offers an anatomy of the failure rather than a remedy.
examples.cn: 她的论文对这次失败作了剖析，而没有给出补救办法。

dict_mnemonic.text: ana（向上、分开）+ tomy（切）→ 分开切开来研究 → 解剖学；身体结构

root: 希腊 ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」→ anatomē「切开、解剖」→ 拉丁 anatomia → 英语 anatomy；同根 atom 意为「不可切的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of cutting: the science, the structure revealed, the cutting itself, metaphorical analysis, the body in speech, plant and animal bodies, institutional structure and the school subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都沿着「切开」这一动作展开：学科、被揭示的结构、切割本身、比喻性的剖析、口语中的身体、动植物身体、机构结构与学校科目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body opened layer by layer, each part labelled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具被逐层打开、每个部件都带标签的身体。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SCIENCE: the physical cutting and the discipline that grew from it.
branches.cn: 动作与学科：实际的切割，以及由它生长出来的学科。

branches.en: WHAT THE CUT REVEALS: human, animal and plant bodies are described part by part.
branches.cn: 切开后所见：人、动物与植物的身体被逐部件描述。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: books, rumours and institutions can be taken apart the same way.
branches.cn: 比喻延伸：书籍、谣言与机构也能以同样方式拆解。

branches.en: THE BODY IN SPEECH: informal use lets the noun stand for the whole body.
branches.cn: 口语中的身体：非正式用法让该名词代指整个身体。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: in medical schools the science becomes a course with examinations.
branches.cn: 科目：在医学院，这门科学变成有考试的课程。

intro.en: Anatomy is a Greek compound: a prefix of opening, the verb 'to cut', and a noun ending. English also uses the combining form -tomy for surgical cuttings.
intro.cn: anatomy 是希腊语复合词：表示打开的动词前缀、动词「切」，以及名词词尾。英语还用构词成分 -tomy 表示外科切开。

latinIntro.en: Latin anatomia came from Greek anatomē. The Latinized form supplies anatomy, anatomical, anatomist and anatomize; the Greek root tom- supplies appendectomy, tonsillectomy and lobotomy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 来自希腊 anatomē；拉丁化形式衍生 anatomy、anatomical、anatomist、anatomize；希腊词根 tom- 衍生 appendectomy、tonsillectomy、lobotomy。

items.meaning: a cutting up; the structure revealed
items.example: The anatomy of the insect was drawn in detail.
items.exampleCN: 这只昆虫的解剖结构被详细绘制。

items.example: The anatomical model comes apart in twelve pieces.
items.exampleCN: 这个解剖模型可拆成十二块。

items.example: The two joints are anatomically identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两个关节在结构上完全相同。

items.example: The anatomist named the muscle in 1840.
items.exampleCN: 这位解剖学家在 1840 年给该肌肉命名。

items.meaning: to dissect or analyse in detail
items.example: He anatomized the argument line by line.
items.exampleCN: 他逐行剖析了这场论证。

items.example: An atom of carbon has six protons.
items.exampleCN: 一个碳原子有六个质子。

items.structure: tomos (a cut, a slice) + English form
items.meaning: a large book, a 'slice' of writing
items.example: The library owns a rare tome on beetles.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆藏有一部罕见的甲虫专著。

items.meaning: a cutting short; a perfect summary
items.example: The small town is the epitome of quiet.
items.exampleCN: 这个小镇是宁静的缩影。

definition_zh: 祖先；祖宗；（事物的）前身
definition_en: a person from whom one is descended, or an earlier thing from which a later one developed
core_image: 泛黄的族谱上，一代代名字向上延伸
scene: 家里的老相册第一页，是一位从南方迁来的曾祖父。Her ancestors came from a fishing village in the south.
sceneCN: 这里 ancestor 是「祖先」（第 1 个义项：血缘上的先辈）；句意是她的祖先来自南方一个渔村。

derivatives.zh: 名词：前身；先行词，同源于拉丁语「在前」

senses.title: A forebear in the family
senses.definition: a person in one's family line who lived long ago
senses.definitionCN: 家族血脉中生活在很久以前的先辈
senses.example: Her ancestors came from a fishing village in the south.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖先来自南方一个渔村。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin antecessor, 'one who goes before', so an ancestor is literally a person who walked ahead of us in time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 antecessor「走在前面的人」，所以祖先字面上就是在时间上走在我们前面的人。

senses.title: An earlier form of a thing
senses.definition: an early version or forerunner from which a later thing developed
senses.definitionCN: 后来事物由之发展而来的早期形态或先驱
senses.example: The abacus is an ancestor of the modern calculator.
senses.exampleCN: 算盘是现代计算器的前身。
senses.why: Once the word means 'what came before', it can be applied to machines and ideas, not only to people, which is common in histories of technology.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「先前存在的东西」，它就能用于机器与观念，而不只用于人，这在技术史中很常见。

intro.en: Ancestor is a Latin 'one who goes before', filtered through French.
intro.cn: ancestor 是拉丁语「走在前面的人」，经法语传入英语。

items.en: ante meant 'before', in place or in time.
items.cn: ante 意为「在前」，指位置或时间。

items.en: cedere meant 'to go, to yield', the verb of movement.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让」，是表示移动的动词。

items.en: antecessor meant 'a predecessor, one who goes before'.
items.cn: antecessor 意为「前任、走在前头的人」。

items.en: French reshaped the word as ancestre, and English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语把词形改造为 ancestre，英语借入。

items.en: English ancestor first meant a family forebear, then extended to forerunners of machines and species.
items.cn: 英语 ancestor 先指家族先辈，后扩展到机器与物种的前身。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ancestry family; the near-meaning group contrasts forebear and descendant.
note.cn: 形近组是 ancestry 词族；近义组对比先辈与后代。

normalIntro.cn: 祖先就是走在我们前面的人。

normal.cn: ancestor 是人，ancestry 是世系。

normal.en: Ancestral home is the family's old place.
normal.cn: ancestral home 指祖居。

normal.en: Machines can have ancestors too.
normal.cn: 机器也可以有「前身」。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-ces-tor.

abstract.en: Picture a family tree climbing upward.
abstract.cn: 想象向上延伸的族谱。

abstract.en: See an old photograph of a great-grandfather.
abstract.cn: 想象一张曾祖父的旧照片。

abstract.en: Imagine an abacus beside a calculator.
abstract.cn: 想象算盘放在计算器旁边。

examples.en: Her ancestors arrived here two centuries ago.
examples.cn: 她的祖先两个世纪前来到这里。

examples.en: Humans and apes share a common ancestor.
examples.cn: 人类与猿类有共同祖先。

examples.en: The steam engine is an ancestor of the modern turbine.
examples.cn: 蒸汽机是现代涡轮机的前身。
